name: Reshaper (Cryptic Archetype)
body:
As cryptics learn about the myriad bizarre patterns that fill the universe, some begin to realize how limited their own forms are. These individuals take to modifying themselves with psionics, assuming wild and powerful new shapes.

Warped Appearance (Ex)

Rather than tattoos, a reshaper’s powers manifest in various physical alterations across her body. The reshaper’s known powers can be identified via Knowledge (dungeoneering or engineering) checks with a DC equal to 15 + double the power’s level. When a cryptic manifests one of her powers, it creates a visual or auditory pattern of energy during the action taken to manifest the pattern. While the reshaper’s powers have the normal displays for psionic powers – auditory, mental, and the like – this pattern unique to the reshaper cannot be suppressed as normal displays can be suppressed.

This ability replaces pattern designs.

Aberrant Restructuring: Whenever she would gain a cryptic insight, a reshaper may instead gain 2 customization points which can be used to select aegis customizations as an aberrant aegis. A reshaper uses her cryptic level as her aberrant level for the purpose of determining what customizations she may select.

Metamorphic Insight

At 7th level, the reshaper adds metamorphosis to her list of powers known. At 16th level, she adds greater metamorphosis to her list of powers known.

This ability replaces the powers known gained at 7th and 16th levels.

Supreme Insight: A reshaper gains access to the following supreme insight: Reshaped Perfection: The reshaper has achieved a bodily pattern which stands above all others. Her type changes to outsider (native), she gains DR 10/psionic, and she treats her manifester level as 4 higher for all manifestations of metamorphosis or greater metamorphosis powers.

Daevic Passions
Fixation

Daevas of Fixation seek out servants with a one-track mind. Daevics of Fixation specialize in ranged combat, employing firearms or similar weapons to kill or incapacitate foes at range. Most often, they play the roles of assassins or infantry, dominating the battlefield either through powerful weapon batteries or more compact handheld firearms. Fixation daevics are the most common type of daevics in militarized industrial societies, making use of their aptitude at long-distance combat to attain many victories.

Passion Veils: Armory of the Conqueror, Courtesan’s Cloak, Daevic Aspect, Gorget of the Wyrm, Hand

Cannons, H.U.D.*, Lashing Spinnerets, Nanite

Cloud*, Micro-Missile Gauntlet*, Pestilence Cloak, Riven Darts, Sentinel’s Helm

Skill(s): Perception, Stealth, Knowledge (geography)

At 3rd level, the daevic gains Precise Shot as a bonus feat.

At 5th level, she gains Deadly Aim and at 8th level she gains Improved Precise Shot or Pinpoint Targeting. The daevic does not need to meet the prerequisites for these feats.

At 6th level, the daeva becomes more refined, driving the daevic towards a particular combat style. Choose one of the following aspects: Cannoneer: Opting for powerful heavy weapons over more compact machines, cannoneers build their combat style around doling out extreme destruction. When fighting using a ranged weapon, all creatures adjacent to the projectile’s point of impact (or line of fire, in the case of spread or automatic or area-damaging weapons) take the minimum amount of damage from the attack, as if they were caught in the radius of a splash weapon (DC is 10 + 1/2 the daevic’s level + her Charisma modifier for half damage). The effective radius of this ability improves to 10 feet at 12th level and 15 feet at 18th level.

Sharpshooter: Employing expert aim and surgical precision to their attacks, sharpshooters aim to annihilate their target in a single shot whenever possible. As a full-round action, a sharpshooter can take careful aim and pool all of her attack potential with a ranged weapon into a single, deadly shot. When she does this, she shoots the weapon at a single target, but makes as many attack rolls as she can, based on her base attack bonus.

She makes the attack rolls in order from highest bonus to lowest, as if she were making a full attack (this applies even to weapons normally incapable of firing more than one shot per round). If any of the attack rolls hit the target, the sharpshooter’s single attack is considered to have hit.

For each additional successful attack roll beyond the first, the sharpshooter increases the damage of the shot by the base damage dice of the weapon.

For instance, if a 7th-level sharpshooter firing a musket hits with both attacks, she does 2d12 points of damage with the shot, instead of 1d12 points of damage, before adding any damage modifiers. Precision damage and extra damage from weapon special abilities (such as flaming) are added with damage modifiers and are not increased by this effect. If one or more rolls are critical threats, she confirms the critical once using her highest base attack bonus –5.

For each critical threat beyond the first, she reduces this penalty by 1 (to a maximum of 0). The sharpshooter only misfires on this shot if all the attack rolls are misfires. She cannot use this effect with a blunderbuss or other scatter weapon when attacking creatures in a cone.

Vigilance

Daevics of Vigilance are unrivaled analysts, tacticians, and spies, able to garner information and channel it effectively towards a variety of strategically salient purposes. Be it finding a crucial weakness in the foe’s defenses or optimizing the functionality of a unit’s own soldiers, Vigilance daevics are an incredible asset to any force that commands them or is capable of otherwise harnessing their intellectual expertise.

Passion Veils: Bloody Shroud, Collar of Skilled

Instruction, Courtesan’s Cloak, Cuirass of Confidence, Daevic Aspect, Dreamcatcher, Essence of the Succubus, H.U.D.*, Sentinel’s Helm

Skill(s): Perception, Knowledge (any two)

At 3rd level, the daevic gains a +2 bonus on all Knowledge checks and may attempt such checks untrained. In addition, she gains the studied target ability of a slayer of her class level. The DCs of daevic class abilities and veils against that opponent increase by the studied target bonus.

At 6th level the daeva becomes more refined, driving the daevic toward a particular combat style. Choose one of the following aspects: Optimizer: Making the most of any situation, optimizers excel at forging a path to victory from any circumstance.

At 6th level, the optimizer gains the use of the strategy class feature, as the tactician class. She learns one strategy at 6th level plus another at 12th and 18th level.

For the purpose of these strategies, the optimizer uses her Charisma modifier in place of her Intelligence modifier and treats all allies within 30 feet and all allies affected by one of her veils as being part of her collective.

Saboteur: Saboteurs specialize in locating and compounding weaknesses within an opponent’s capabilities. At 6th level, the daevic gains sneak attack 1d6, alongside the debilitating injury ability of an unchained rogue PFU. At 12th and 18th level, the daevic gains an additional die of sneak attack as well as the ability to apply an additional debilitating injury effect on the target whenever the ability is used.

Retold daevic

The Daevic passions and Daevic Aspect options presented in this book are designed to be compatible with the original Daevic class published in Akashic

Mysteries. A revised version of the class exists in the form of the Retold Daevic, which has its own versions of the passions presented here.

Dissident Strife: mortality vs eternity

This strife posits the value of the timely vs. the value of the timeless. Should a person focus on the needs and desires of the people around them or seek higher truth amidst fundamental structures of existence? Is the value of one’s actions defined by the legacy they leave behind or by the experiences they create in the moment? Mortality focuses on direct action with little care for consequences, emphasizing quick movements and decisive strikes to resolve immediate conflicts. Eternity focuses on a more defensive and distant suite of abilities, mitigating oncoming damage and hampering enemy action to encourage steady and patient resolution.

Strife Benefit: As long as the dissident is attuned to mortality, she adds her strife bonus as an insight bonus on damage rolls. In addition, all of her movement speeds increase by 10 feet for every point of her strife bonus.

As long as the dissident is attuned to eternity, she adds her strife bonus as an insight bonus on Reflex saves and gains DR/- equal to her strife bonus. This stacks with all other forms of damage reduction.

Unique Conflict: Whenever a creature within close range of the dissident is reduced to 0 hit points, she can spend an immediate action to shift one step towards mortality.

Whenever a creature within close range of the dissident recovers an amount of hit points equal to or greater than twice the dissident’s level, she can spend an immediate action to shift one step towards eternity.

Nuances: A dissident with the mortality and eternity strife can choose from the following nuances:

Armaments of Tribulation (requires dissident 9, manifest equilibrium): In place of the normal bonus granted by the manifest equilibrium nuance, she can grant the imbued armament the following special abilities: Mortality: vicious (weapon), sacrificial (armor)

Eternity: preventative (weapon), stanching (armor)

Balance: decisive (weapon), selfless (armor) Additionally, the bonus granted to an imbued object that she summons using manifest equilibrium increases to a +1 enhancement bonus, +1 per 5 dissident levels she possesses.

Burnout (requires dissident 6): When the dissident uses a roar of existence while completely attuned, she may become balanced in her struggle as part of using it. If she does, she does not need to spend a spell point and creatures in the area are not allowed a saving throw against the roar’s initial effect. If you possess the lingering echo nuance, targets are still allowed a saving throw against the effects of that ability.

Challenge Perpetuity (requires dissident 9) (Su) Whenever the dissident positively impacts a creature with confront motives, they also gain the benefits of the dissident’s current strife benefit (using her current strife bonus) for the duration. Whenever the dissident successfully negatively impacts a creature with confront motives, they gain an additional effect depending on the dissident’s attunement: if she is attuned to mortality, the creature takes a -4 penalty to AC, magic skill checks, and concentration checks for the duration. If she is attuned to eternity, the creature takes a -4 penalty to attack rolls and Reflex saves for the duration.

Guided Roar (requires dissident 6): When the dissident uses roar of existence while completely attuned, she may have it take the form of a close-range cone, a medium-range line, or a burst of normal size centered within close range. Alternatively, the dissident may move up to her movement speed when using roar of existence without provoking attacks of opportunity, affecting all enemies who are adjacent to her at any point in the movement with roar of existence.

Lingering Echo (requires dissident 6): Any creature who fails their save against the dissident’s roar of existence becomes blinded (for roar of finality) or staggered and entangled (for roar of infinity) for 1 round. This duration improves to a number of rounds equal to the dissident’s operative modifier if the dissident is completely attuned. In addition, any enemy who ends their turn in an area where roar of existence was used within a number of rounds equal to the dissident’s ability modifier takes 1d8 points of damage per 4 dissident levels (Will save negates).

Of Mortals and Mysteries (requires dissident 6): When the dissident gains this nuance, she chooses a single agent ploy and either a single cleric domain or a single inquisitor inquisition. While the dissident is attuned to mortality, she gains the chosen ploy’s feature and can use its devious technique against any target who could normally be targeted by a discerning strike. When the dissident is attuned to eternity, she gains the chosen domain or inquisition’s 1st-level ability, using her casting ability modifier in place of her Wisdom for determining the effects of any domain or inquisition abilities.

The dissident can choose this nuance an additional time at 9th level or higher in dissident. When chosen a second time, she gains the benefits of the conspiratorial ploy and always a clue features of the ploy while attuned to mortality, and the 6th- or 8th-level domain or inquisition ability while attuned to eternity.

Strife Dedication At 4th level, the dissident can spend a spell point to unleash a roar of existence as a standard action. The roar is a 5-foot radius burst centered on herself.

This burst radius increases by 5 feet for every 4 dissident levels beyond 4th. The effect of roar of existence is based on the dissident’s attunement. The dissident is not affected by her own roar.

Roar of Finality: A dissident attuned to mortality deals 1d6 points of damage per dissident level to creatures in the area (Reflex save half). This damage type is either acid, cold, electricity, or fire, chosen when the dissident gains this ability.

Roar of Infinity: A dissident attuned to eternity causes all targets in the area to fall prone (Reflex save negates). If creatures in the area are airborne, they descend up to 600 feet and land prone if they hit the ground, taking falling damage as normal.

Roar of Uncertainty: A balanced dissident causes all targets in the area to be pushed 5 feet away from you, plus an additional 5 feet per 4 dissident levels beyond 4th (Reflex save negates). The area of the roar of uncertainty becomes difficult terrain for 1 round.

Strife Devotion (Su)

At 13th level, while the dissident is completely attuned to mortality, her movement speed bonus increases to 40 feet plus an additional 10 feet for every 3 levels beyond 13th she possesses. In addition, the dissident may spend a move action to attempt a new saving throw against any effect on her.

While the dissident is completely attuned to eternity, her DR/- increases to half her dissident level and she gains fast healing equal to 1/4 her dissident level. This fast healing cannot heal the dissident above half her normal hit points.

Strife Mastery (Su)

While the dissident is completely attuned to mortality, she gains an additional move or swift action each round. Whenever the dissident attacks or uses a sphere effect, she may take a 5-foot step (this does not count towards the number of 5-foot steps she may make per turn, nor does it detract from her movement).

While the dissident is completely attuned to eternity, she gains an additional immediate action and may make any number of attacks of opportunity each round. Whenever the dissident attacks, uses a sphere effect, or uses roar of infinity, she may perform a bull rush, drag, or reposition combat maneuver against any affected targets.
